This audit identified 0 duplicate tax number(s) affecting 0 customer account(s), and 4,628 customer(s) with a missing or invalid tax number. Finance review and corrective action are required before these records can be used reliably in AR processing.

2. Methodology

Data source: Local MongoDB customers collection. All data is synced from Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365FO) by the Middleware sync process. This report reflects the state of the local copy at the time of generation.

Tax number field: taxExemptNumber (Mongoose schema field mapped from the D365FO TaxExemptNumber entity attribute).

Normalisation logic: Before duplicate detection, each tax number is normalised by (1) trimming leading and trailing whitespace, and (2) collapsing any internal run of whitespace characters to a single space. Dashes, dots, slashes, and other punctuation are preserved because they carry structural meaning in many regional tax-number formats. The original stored value is always shown alongside the normalised form.

Missing tax number detection: A tax number is considered missing if it is null, undefined, an empty string, a whitespace-only string, or one of the known placeholder values: N/A, NA, -, --, 0 (case-insensitive). These placeholders are configurable in the script source (PLACEHOLDER_VALUES_LOWER).

Movement detection: Movement status is reported as "Unknown — not enough local data" for all customers. The local MongoDB stores batch-processing records (data_enhanced_records, data_source_records) with payloads in a generic data: Record<string, any> field whose internal structure varies by entry-processor type and is not typed in schema definitions. Extracting a reliable customer account reference from those payloads would require entry-processor–specific logic that cannot safely generalise across all processors. See Section 5 — Technical Notes for details and recommended next steps.

No duplicate tax numbers were found.

5. Recommended Finance Actions

The following actions are recommended based on this audit. The Development Team will not change any master data or transaction data without explicit Finance confirmation.

Duplicate Tax Numbers

  • Duplicate tax numbers cause ambiguity during AR processing: when the middleware searches customers by tax number, multiple records are returned, which prevents reliable invoice and payment matching.
  • For each duplicate group, Finance should identify the canonical customer record and determine whether the duplicates are data-entry errors, merged entities, or distinct customers incorrectly sharing a tax number.
  • If a duplicate customer has no movements, Finance should consider requesting its removal or deactivation in D365FO.
  • If a duplicate customer has movements, it must not be deleted. Finance should review whether a master-data merge or tax-number correction is appropriate in D365FO.
  • Because movement detection is currently unavailable locally (see Technical Notes), Finance should verify movement status directly in D365FO before taking action.

Customers Missing Tax Numbers

  • Customers without a valid tax number cannot be correctly matched during AR processing and may cause tax-reporting gaps.
  • Finance should provide the correct tax number for each listed customer, or confirm whether the customer is exempt and document the exemption.
  • Once confirmed, the Development Team can coordinate with the D365FO administrator to update the record, which will be re-synced to the middleware automatically.

6. Technical Notes

Movement Detection Limitation

The local MongoDB does not currently expose a reliable, schema-typed link between a specific customer account and its processed/posted transaction records. The available collections are:

  • data_batches — tracks processing batch jobs by company and entry-processor type, but does not store per-customer-account line data.
  • data_enhanced_records and data_source_records — store the raw payload in a generic data: Record<string, any> field whose internal structure varies by entry-processor type (AR, cash-in, cash-out, closing, etc.) and is not defined in schema types accessible to a standalone script.

Attempting to scan the generic data field for customer account strings would risk false positives and false negatives. Until a typed projection or a dedicated index of customer-to-batch linkage is implemented, movement status cannot be determined locally and is marked as "Unknown — not enough local data".

Recommendation: Finance should verify movement status directly in D365FO (Accounts Receivable > Customers > Customer Transactions) for any customer account flagged in this report before requesting removal or deactivation.

Script Safety

This script is read-only. It opens a MongoDB connection, runs aggregation and find queries only, writes a local HTML file, and disconnects. It does not call any D365FO API, does not modify any document, and does not enqueue any background jobs.

Re-running the Report

The report reflects the state of the local MongoDB at the time of generation. After Finance actions have been taken and the sync has run, re-run pnpm customer-tax-audit to generate a fresh report and confirm the issues have been resolved.

Normalisation Constants

The following placeholder values are treated as missing tax numbers (in addition to null / empty string): N/A, NA, -, --, 0. To adjust this list, edit the PLACEHOLDER_VALUES_LOWER constant in the script source file.
